blocks.content: The Constitution is the supreme law of the land, and all organs of the State derive their authority and jurisdiction from it.

rows: Courts can strike down unconstitutional laws
Courts cannot strike down Parliamentary statutes
Limited by the Basic Structure Doctrine

items: Differentiate between Parliamentary Sovereignty (UK) and Constitutional Supremacy (India) for Prelims.
Kesavananda Bharati (1973) established that Article 368 does not enable Parliament to alter the basic structure of the Constitution.
Article 13 provides the explicit constitutional basis for judicial review in India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution is the ultimate source of power for the Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary in India.
Under Article 13, any law enacted by Parliament or state legislatures that violates Fundamental Rights is void.
The Basic Structure Doctrine limits Parliament's amending power under Article 368 to preserve constitutional principles.
Indian federalism enforces Constitutional Supremacy to maintain division of powers between the Centre and States.
